context.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a globally distributed e-commerce platform built to handle physical and electronic book sales, recommendations, and reviews. It delivers high scalability, strict security compliance, and multi-currency support across multiple geographic regions.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Customer (Shopper), Registered Customer/Reviewer, Site Administrator/Content Moderator.
- **External Systems:** Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal), Third-Party Shipping APIs (FedEx/UPS), Identity Provider (Auth0/AWS Cognito), Notification Service, and Supplier Feeds/ERP.
- **Containers:** AWS CloudFront / Global Accelerator (CDN/Edge), API Gateway with AWS WAF, AWS ECS/EKS Containerized Microservices (Catalog, Cart/Checkout, Recommendations), and Regional Databases.

## Relationships
- **Customer to CDN:** HTTPS / TLS 1.3
- **CDN to API Gateway:** HTTPS
- **Microservices to Identity Provider:** OAuth2 / OIDC over HTTPS
- **API Gateway to Payment Gateway & Shipping APIs:** HTTPS / REST
- **Online Bookstore to Notification Service:** HTTPS / REST Webhooks
- **Supplier Feeds to Online Bookstore:** Secure SFTP / S3 Batch Drops
- **Internal Microservices:** Mutual TLS (mTLS) via Service Mesh (Istio / AWS App Mesh)

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Infrastructure:** AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) for multi-region redundancy and low global latency.
- **Edge Delivery:** AWS CloudFront and Global Accelerator to satisfy the sub-2-second 3G page load requirement.
- **Compute:** AWS ECS/EKS for containerized microservices deployment with multi-AZ resilience.
- **Security & Compliance:** AWS WAF, AWS KMS (Customer Managed Keys), AWS Secrets Manager, and client-side tokenization (Stripe Elements) for PCI-DSS scope reduction.
- **Observability:** OpenTelemetry for centralized distributed tracing and multi-region log aggregation.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages a globally distributed, containerized microservices pattern on AWS to guarantee 99.95% availability and sub-2-second performance for 1 million MAU. Security controls, multi-region data residency strategies, and decoupled third-party integrations ensure full GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
• An Amazon-style online bookstore providing catalog browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations for 1M MAU.
• Designed for high availability (99.95% uptime) across three AWS regions while enforcing GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
• Shopper, Registered Customer, Site Administrator, and Business Analyst
• React/TypeScript Single Page Application (SPA)
• AWS API Gateway
• Catalog & Search Container (Go/gRPC, Amazon OpenSearch, Aurora PostgreSQL)
• Order & Checkout Container (Node.js/Spring Boot, isolated Aurora PostgreSQL cluster)
• Recommendation Engine (Python/FastAPI)
• Customer Reviews & Ratings Container (Python/FastAPI, Amazon DynamoDB)
• External Payment Gateway and Third-Party Shipping APIs

## Relationships
• SPA interacts with API Gateway via HTTPS/JSON
• API Gateway routes requests to internal containers via gRPC over mTLS
• Order & Checkout container communicates with Payment Gateway and Shipping APIs via HTTPS/REST
• Recommendation Engine asynchronously consumes order events

## Technology Stack
• AWS ECS with Fargate for scalable container orchestration
• Amazon CloudFront and S3 for global static asset delivery
• Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and DynamoDB for persistent storage
• AWS WAF and AWS Secrets Manager for security and compliance

## Rationale
• Microservices and managed AWS services ensure scalability to 1M MAU while meeting the <2s page load SLA on 3G.
• Strict network isolation and IAM least-privilege boundaries protect sensitive PII and isolate PCI-DSS scope.

Single Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
The Single Page Application (SPA) container serves as the primary browser-based user interface for the Online Bookstore, delivering a global, sub-2-second catalog browsing and secure checkout experience. It leverages a modern frontend stack deployed via AWS to support 1 million monthly active users with high performance and security.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application (SPA) container
- Routing & Shell Component (React Router, Zustand)
- Catalog & Search Component
- Checkout & Cart Component
- Recommendation & Reviews Component
- Admin & Analytics Dashboard Component
- API Client Layer (Axios/Fetch with OpenAPI SDK)

## Relationships
- Shopper / Registered Customer / Admin -> Single Page Application (SPA): Interacts with UI [HTTPS / JSON]
- Single Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway: Sends client requests and API calls [HTTPS / JSON]
- Routing & Shell Component -> Functional Components: Renders views [In-memory]
- Functional Components -> API Client Layer: Executes remote operations [HTTPS / JSON]

## Technology Stack
- React & TypeScript: Core frontend framework for type-safe component development
- Amazon CloudFront & S3: Global static asset delivery for sub-2-second page loads (R-06)
- Zustand: Decoupled global state management, including local cart persistence for resilience
- AWS Lambda@Edge: Enforces Content Security Policy (CSP), HSTS, and CORS for OWASP Top-10 mitigation (R-08)

## Rationale
This component-level architecture ensures lightning-fast global performance and high availability while strictly separating untrusted client-side execution from secure backend services. The modular design protects conversion rates through resilient cart handling and robust client-side security controls.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system is a scalable e-commerce platform designed for purchasing physical and electronic books with integrated recommendations, reviews, and secure global checkout. The architecture utilizes an edge-optimized API Gateway to route client traffic securely while supporting multi-region scalability and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application (SPA): React and TypeScript client hosted on Amazon S3 and CloudFront.
- API Gateway: AWS API Gateway serving as the primary trust boundary and entry point.
- Edge Router / Reverse Proxy: Amazon CloudFront handling TLS 1.3 termination, caching, and OpenAPI schema validation.
- Auth & Policy Enforcer: Component validating JWT tokens, managing rate limiting, and enforcing OWASP Top-10 security controls (R-08).
- Request Transformer / Geo-Resolver: Component extracting client geo-location and injecting multi-currency headers (USD, EUR, GBP).
- Resiliency & Fallback Orchestrator: Component handling circuit breaking, timeouts, and fallback payloads.
- Backend Containers: Catalog & Search, Order & Checkout, Recommendation Engine, and Customer Reviews & Ratings containers.
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Notification Service, and Supplier Feeds/ERP.

## Relationships
- SPA -> API Gateway: Sends client requests via HTTPS / JSON.
- API Gateway -> Catalog & Search Container: Routes catalogue and search requests via gRPC over mTLS.
- API Gateway -> Order & Checkout Container: Routes order and checkout requests via gRPC over mTLS.
- API Gateway -> Recommendation Engine: Routes recommendation queries via gRPC over mTLS.
- API Gateway -> Customer Reviews & Ratings Container: Routes review and rating requests via gRPC over mTLS.
- API Gateway -> External Systems: Integrates with payment gateways and third-party shipping APIs via secure REST/HTTPS protocols.

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Infrastructure: AWS deployed across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` regions for global reach and 99.95% uptime (R-07).
- Edge & Routing: AWS API Gateway and Amazon CloudFront for regional endpoint routing and response caching.
- Security & Compliance: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for mTLS certificate rotation, AWS X-Ray for distributed tracing, and AWS CloudWatch Synthetix for canary monitoring.
- Infrastructure as Code: Terraform and AWS CDK managed via GitOps pipelines.

## Rationale
This multi-region serverless architecture meets the 1M MAU scalability requirement (R-05) and sub-2-second page load SLA on 3G networks (R-06) through edge caching and geo-routing. Centralizing security, rate limiting, and resiliency logic at the API Gateway ensures robust GDPR/CCPA compliance and protection against OWASP Top-10 vulnerabilities (R-08).

Catalog & Search Container.analysis:
## Overview
- The Catalog & Search Container powers high-performance product browsing, keyword search, and localized pricing for the Online Bookstore.
- It delivers a scalable, low-latency search experience designed to handle 1M MAU globally across AWS regions.

## Key Elements
- Search API Handler (`Go`)
- Catalog Management Service (`Go`)
- Index Synchronizer (`Go` / `AWS Lambda`)
- Product Read Model Cache (`Redis`)
- Localization & Currency Resolver (`Go`)
- Search Analytics Emitter (`Go`)
- Amazon OpenSearch
- Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon Kinesis

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search API Handler [gRPC over mTLS]
- Search API Handler -> Amazon OpenSearch [REST/HTTPS]
- Catalog Management Service -> Aurora PostgreSQL [SQL/TCP]
- Index Synchronizer -> Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon OpenSearch [CDC/Debezium]
- Search API Handler -> Product Read Model Cache [TCP/Redis Protocol]
- Search API Handler -> Localization & Currency Resolver [Internal gRPC]
- Search Analytics Emitter -> Amazon Kinesis [Async/TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency concurrency in search and ingestion handlers.
- Amazon OpenSearch: Provides typo-tolerant keyword search and advanced filtering.
- Aurora PostgreSQL: Acts as the primary relational source of truth with multi-region replication.
- Redis: Powers low-latency product read caching and currency rate lookups.
- Amazon Kinesis: Enables asynchronous, non-blocking telemetry and search analytics streaming.
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Manages containerized microservice deployments with auto-scaling.

## Rationale
- Decoupling reads from writes via asynchronous CDC indexing ensures sub-2s performance under heavy load.
- Multi-region replication and resilient circuit-breakers guarantee 99.95% uptime and global scalability.

Order & Checkout Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Order & Checkout Container manages secure transactions, multi-currency pricing, and fulfillment for the Online Bookstore system. It ensures high availability, strict security, and fault-tolerant checkout workflows.]

## Key Elements
* Checkout Controller
* Cart & Pricing Engine
* Order Orchestrator
* Payment Gateway Client
* Shipping & Fulfillment Client
* Event Publisher
* Order Repository

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Checkout Controller (gRPC over mTLS)
* Checkout Controller -> Cart & Pricing Engine & Order Orchestrator (In-process Java method calls)
* Order Orchestrator -> Payment Gateway Client & Shipping & Fulfillment Client (HTTPS / REST with Resilience4j Circuit Breakers)
* Order Orchestrator & Event Publisher -> Order Repository (JDBC / JPA over TLS 1.3)
* Event Publisher -> AWS EventBridge / Kafka (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
* Java 21 / Spring Boot: Core runtime for enterprise-grade dependency injection and container logic
* Aurora PostgreSQL: ACID-compliant relational database for transactional data integrity
* HikariCP & AWS RDS Proxy: Database connection pooling and spike mitigation
* Resilience4j: Circuit breakers and fault tolerance for external API calls
* AWS Secrets Manager: Secure credential storage and automated secret rotation
* AWS EventBridge / Kafka: Asynchronous messaging with Dead Letter Queues (DLQ)

## Rationale
[This architecture uses the Saga pattern and Transactional Outbox to guarantee reliable distributed transactions and prevent dual-write failures. It decouples core checkout processes from external dependencies while enforcing strict security, PCI-DSS scope reduction, and 99.95% availability.]

Recommendation Engine.analysis:
## Overview
[The Recommendation Engine container within the Online Bookstore platform generates personalized 'Customers also bought' product suggestions while strictly enforcing GDPR/CCPA data minimization and high-availability constraints. It securely processes asynchronous order events to deliver low-latency recommendations across multi-region cloud environments.]

## Key Elements
- **API Router**: Python FastAPI component exposing gRPC endpoints for recommendation queries with Pydantic schema validation.
- **Inference Pipeline**: Python PyTorch component computing personalized matrix factorization models with signed artifact integrity.
- **Event Consumer**: Python Kafka consumer ingesting anonymized order events via Amazon MSK.
- **Fallback & Caching Manager**: Redis instance caching global trending sets and handling fallback states.
- **Business Rules & Merchandising Filter**: Python component evaluating local stock state replicas and suppression rules.

## Relationships
- **API Gateway -> API Router**: Routes recommendation queries via gRPC over mTLS.
- **Order & Checkout Container -> Event Consumer**: Emits asynchronous order events via Amazon MSK.
- **API Router -> Business Rules Filter -> Fallback & Caching Manager**: Evaluates candidate lists via in-process calls and Redis protocol.
- **Business Rules Filter -> Local Stock Cache**: Validates item availability using asynchronously replicated state.

## Technology Stack
- **Python & FastAPI**: Chosen for rapid service development and robust asynchronous request handling.
- **PyTorch**: Used for scalable machine learning inference and matrix factorization.
- **Amazon MSK (Kafka)**: Provides decoupled, high-throughput asynchronous event streaming.
- **Redis**: Enables sub-50ms caching for fallback and trending recommendations.
- **Amazon ECS with Fargate**: Delivers containerized, auto-scaling compute across AWS regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`).

## Rationale
[This architecture uses decoupled asynchronous event streams and local caching to maintain 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page loads under peak traffic. Strict pseudonymization and localized rule validation ensure GDPR and CCPA compliance without compromising system performance or availability.]

Customer Reviews & Ratings Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Microservice container managing customer reviews, 5-star ratings, helpful votes, and moderation for the online bookstore.
- Designed for high write-availability, low-latency reads, and global scalability to support 1M MAU.

## Key Elements
- **Review API Router:** FastAPI component handling HTTP/gRPC requests, JWT validation, and Pydantic input sanitization.
- **Moderation Service:** Automated NLP/AWS Comprehend pipeline for profanity and sentiment filtering.
- **Vote Processor:** Isolated component handling atomic helpful votes and anti-sybil checks.
- **Rating Aggregator:** Asynchronous background worker using AWS SQS.
- **Review Data Access Layer:** Boto3 client interfacing with Amazon DynamoDB.
- **Read Caching Layer:** Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) cluster.
- **Infrastructure:** AWS ECS with AWS Fargate across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Review API Router: Routes requests via gRPC over mTLS
- Review API Router -> Moderation Service: Internal in-memory calls
- Review API Router -> Vote Processor: Internal in-memory calls
- Vote Processor & Review Data Access Layer -> Amazon DynamoDB: TCP over AWS PrivateLink with KMS encryption
- Rating Aggregator -> AWS SQS: Asynchronous messaging
- Review Data Access Layer -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Read-through caching over TLS

## Technology Stack
- **Python / FastAPI:** High-performance asynchronous API framework with native Pydantic schema validation.
- **Amazon DynamoDB:** NoSQL database with Global Tables and Global Secondary Indexes (`BookID-HelpfulVotes-Index`, `BookID-Rating-Index`) for sub-50ms queries.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis):** In-memory caching for aggregated ratings to maintain <2s page loads.
- **AWS SQS:** Asynchronous event queue preventing write-lock contention.
- **AWS ECS / Fargate:** Serverless container orchestration for multi-region deployment.
- **AWS KMS:** Encryption at rest for GDPR/CCPA compliance and data protection.

## Rationale
- Decouples review writes, rating aggregation, and helpful voting using asynchronous queues and isolated components to prevent performance degradation under peak load.
- Combines DynamoDB Global Tables, Redis caching, and multi-region Fargate deployment to ensure 99.95% availability, strict global compliance, and sub-second response times.
